meta.note: Single source of truth for the skill exam. Every must_include claim is sourced from a verified reference file (see `source`). Do NOT add a claim you cannot trace to a reference or installed typings — a wrong answer key silently inverts the eval. must_not entries are regexes that ONLY appear in wrong answers (safe for a fast pre-fail); semantic negatives are encoded as positive must_include claims instead.

axes.api: API understanding — signatures, what exists / what was removed
axes.react: Solid vs React — does the model drag React reflexes over
axes.v1: Solid 2.0 vs 1.x — does the model fall back to 1.x APIs

questions.title: createEffect signature
questions.prompt: Describe the signature of `createEffect`: how many callbacks it takes, what each one is for, and what happens if you pass a single callback. One short paragraph plus a 3-line example.
must_include: createEffect takes TWO functions: a compute and an apply (plus an optional options object)
compute runs tracked (records reactive deps) and returns a value; apply runs the side effect, is untracked, and may return a cleanup function
the single-callback form (one function only) is a HARD ERROR — it throws synchronously in dev (MISSING_EFFECT_FN) and the one-argument overload is TS-deprecated (never); it is invalid in 2.0
questions.source: reactivity.md:24-50; SKILL.md rule 2

questions.title: reads lag writes
questions.prompt: Right after calling `setCount(1)`, what does `count()` return on the very next line, and why? How do you force the new value to be readable synchronously?
must_include: count() still returns the OLD value (0) on the next line — writes are batched on a microtask, reads return the last committed value
flush() drains the queue synchronously so the read sees the new value
questions.source: reactivity.md:5-22

questions.title: async data without createResource
questions.prompt: How do you load data asynchronously by id and render it while showing a spinner during loading? Name the primitive and the boundary.
must_include: async is just a computation: createMemo(() => fetchX(id())) returns a Promise, and consumers read the accessor normally (the 'no createResource' negative is enforced by the FORBIDDEN list, not this claim)
wrap consumers in a <Loading fallback={...}> boundary; loading state is structural, not a T|undefined hole
questions.source: async-and-actions.md:5-29, 117-124

questions.title: loadingValue and seedLoadingValue
questions.prompt: Contrast `loadingValue` on an async memo with `seedLoadingValue: true` on a derived store. What do consumers, `<Loading>`, and `isPending` observe before the first answer, what happens on later refetches, and how do declared versus bare `ssrSource: "client"` forms render?
must_include: loadingValue gives a memo/signal-family derived source a committed first value; seedLoadingValue: true makes a derived store's seed that committed first value
before the first real answer the source reads as settled: it does not suspend <Loading>, hold a transition, or make isPending(source) true — first-load UI must branch on the provisional value itself
after the first answer lands the provisional value leaves the lineage forever; later refetches use ordinary stale-value/pending semantics
the memo loadingValue is also the compute's first prev

with ssrSource client, a declared loading/seed value renders as commit #0 on the server and through hydration; a bare client source is a structural hole that suspends the nearest Loading fallback and is an error outside a boundary
questions.source: async-and-actions.md loadingValue / seedLoadingValue section

questions.title: async generator memo — yield vs return
questions.prompt: In a `createMemo(async function* () { … })`, what does each `yield` do to the memo's value, and what does `return value` do? Then contrast `return` here with `return` inside an `action(async function*)`.
must_include: in a createMemo async generator each `yield` COMMITS a new value — the accessor updates on every yield, so the memo streams values over time
`return value` ENDS the stream and the returned value is DISCARDED (never committed); the last yielded value stays — `return` is for stopping, not for emitting a final value
in an `action(async function*)` it is the opposite: the generator's `return` value IS the action's result, and `yield` there is a transaction-safe suspension point rather than a committed value
questions.source: async-and-actions.md async generator and action sections

questions.title: uncaught error halts reactivity
questions.prompt: A fetch inside a memo throws and no `<Errored>` / error boundary catches it. Users report the whole app 'freezes' — later button clicks and state updates do nothing. What happened at the reactive-system level, what is the fix, and can `resetErrorHalt` recover it in production?
must_include: an uncaught error that escapes EVERY boundary PERMANENTLY halts reactivity (REACTIVITY_HALTED): it rethrows as an uncaught exception, then all further writes and flushes are silently ignored — it is an app crash with no automatic recovery
the fix is to wrap the fallible reactive code in an error boundary (createErrorBoundary / <Errored>) — a boundary that handles the error keeps the system alive; you do not defuse the halt
resetErrorHalt is re-exported from solid-js for tests/dev tooling; the browser render() and refresh runtime revive a halt in dev, but production remains a hard crash and the server export is a no-op
questions.source: reactivity.md uncaught errors section; dev diagnostics table

questions.title: effect error handler arm
questions.prompt: In `createEffect(compute, { effect, error })`, the `error` handler: (1) can it set a signal to record the message, (2) does it receive the original error object so `instanceof MyError` works, (3) does it catch an exception thrown inside the `effect` (apply) arm? Explain the phase and scope it runs in.
must_include: the error handler runs in the effect phase's imperative, WRITABLE scope — setting a signal to record the error is legal there (it does NOT trip REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE); it is queued on the same schedule as the effect arm
it receives the ORIGINAL thrown error, not an internal wrapper, so instanceof / class branching works

it catches COMPUTE-phase errors only (a throw in compute, or an async source rejection); an error thrown inside the effect/apply arm is NOT routed here — it goes to the enclosing error boundary, so guard the apply body yourself
questions.source: reactivity.md:52-78

questions.title: async-gen action uncaught error + resolve rejection
questions.prompt: Inside an `action(async function* () { … })`, an awaited server call rejects and nothing catches it. Does the app freeze? What happens to the returned promise and to the optimistic writes? Separately: if you `await resolve(() => user())` and the underlying source rejected, what do you get back?
must_include: an uncaught error in an async-generator action REJECTS the returned promise and completes the transition, so the optimistic writes revert and the caller can `.catch` — it does NOT halt reactivity
a try/catch around the yield/await still handles an awaited rejection locally
resolve(() => user()) REJECTS with the source's own error if the source rejected
questions.source: async-and-actions.md action errors and latest/resolve/refresh sections

questions.title: action invocation scope guard
questions.prompt: A component defines `const save = action(async function* () { await api.save(); yield; setSaved(true); })` and then calls `save()` directly in the component body (or from a memo compute). Is that legal? Where should the call live, and what failure is the guard preventing?
must_include: DEFINING the action during component setup is fine, but INVOKING it synchronously from an owned scope (component body, memo/effect compute) throws in dev with ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE
invoke it from an event handler, effect apply/error callback, onSettled/tracked effect, or another IMPERATIVE scope

starting an action is a transaction-starting write; without the guard, a computation tracking what the action writes can LIVELOCK: each write retriggers the compute and starts a replacement transition before the value commits
questions.source: async-and-actions.md action section; reactivity.md no writes or action calls section

questions.title: falsy error identity and nested boundaries
questions.prompt: What values reach user code for `Promise.reject(null)` under `<Errored>` / an effect `error` arm, and for an action generator that `throw undefined` — does the returned action Promise resolve or reject? Also, in `<Errored outer><Loading><Errored inner>...</Errored></Loading></Errored>`, which boundary catches an error from the inner content?
must_include: error identity is exact even for nullish/falsy values: Promise.reject(null) reaches err() and the effect error arm as null, not an internal StatusError wrapper
an action generator that throws undefined REJECTS its returned promise with undefined — it does not resolve successfully; do not infer success from error truthiness
the INNER Errored catches its content even through the intervening Loading; boundaries consume and forward independent status dimensions
questions.source: async-and-actions.md action errors and Errors one path sections; reactivity.md effect error handling section

questions.title: empty async iterator settlement
questions.prompt: A memo uses `createMemo(async function* () { return finalValue; })` and never yields. Does its `<Loading>` fallback stay forever, and does `finalValue` become the memo value? What should the generator do to publish a final value?
must_include: an async iterator that completes without yielding settles the memo to undefined, so Loading RELEASES instead of remaining forever
the generator's return value is DISCARDED for a memo — finalValue does not become the accessor value
use yield finalValue to commit/publish the final value
questions.source: async-and-actions.md async generator section

questions.title: createReaction re-arm replacement
questions.prompt: For `const track = createReaction(cb); track(() => a()); track(() => b());`, both track calls happen before either source changes. What happens when `a` changes and then `b` changes? Is the reaction persistent, and how is it armed for another cycle?
must_include: the second track call REPLACES the first arm; changing a does nothing, then changing b fires cb exactly once
createReaction is one-shot: the callback fires on the next invalidation and the reaction disarms
call track(...) again — commonly inside cb — to arm the next cycle
questions.source: reactivity.md createReaction section

questions.title: affects(target, key?) signature and semantics
questions.prompt: What does `affects(target, key?)` do, and what is its exact signature? Can you call `affects(state, "user", "name")` to mark one nested slot two levels deep? Does marking a store with `affects(store)` cover records added to it after the call?
must_include: affects(target, key?) takes an accessor/Store target and AT MOST ONE optional key — affects(store) marks every record reachable from the store, affects(record, key) marks exactly one named slot of that record

affects(state, "user", "name") is a type error — a three-argument call: keys do not form a path like a 1.x store path (which would ambiguously mark sibling slots); mark several slots with several calls, or target the nested record directly
the mark is snapshot-at-declaration: affects(store) covers only records reachable from the store at the moment of the call — records added to the store afterward are NOT covered
questions.source: async-and-actions.md affects section

questions.title: server function validation must live in the body, not a wrapper
questions.prompt: You write `export const getUser = withValidation(userIdSchema, async (id) => { "use server"; return db.users.find(id); })`, hoping `withValidation` rejects bad ids before the function body runs. Does that work? Why or why not, and where must the check actually live? Also contrast wrapping an export in a module-level `use server` file.
must_include: no — a wrapper wraps the reference, not the registered function: registerServerReference(id, fn) registers the RAW inner function for HTTP dispatch before any wrapper runs, so wrapper-position code like withValidation can only affect the client transport, never the actual HTTP dispatch path

arguments are untrusted input at the dispatch path regardless of the TypeScript types on the reference; validation/auth/rate-limiting must be lines of code INSIDE the function body itself — there is no core/router validation helper
a wrapped export in a module-level use server file is a COMPILE ERROR; put the directive inside the wrapped function so the wrapper can compose around each build's reference
questions.source: server-functions.md directive and trust-boundary section

questions.title: server function metadata: .GET / .withOptions removed
questions.prompt: Can you read `getUser.GET` or call `getUser.withOptions({...})` on a server function reference to check/configure its HTTP method? If not, what replaced them?
must_include: no — the .GET proxy getter and .withOptions(init) are REMOVED with no compatibility shim

declare the method with the GET(fn) wrapper (needs no compiler support, since a function-level "use server" round-trips the wrapper call) and attach arbitrary metadata with withMeta(fn, meta), which shallow-merges and composes with GET in either order
GET(fn) additionally permits HTTP GET but does not disable POST; a GET request to a function without GET is rejected with 405
read metadata back structurally with getServerFunctionMetadata(fn) / isServerFunction(fn) — registered-symbol-brand detection, not property sniffing like the old fn.GET
session-dynamic transport concerns (like a rotating auth header) belong in prepareRequest, a client-side hook that runs before every outgoing call — not in declaration-time metadata
questions.source: server-functions.md GET withMeta and prepareRequest sections

questions.title: respond/redirect/reload and isResponseEnvelope
questions.prompt: A login server function does `if (bad) return respond({ error: 'bad' }, { status: 401 }); return redirect('/dashboard');`. What do `respond`/`redirect`/`reload` actually return, and how should client code detect that a return value is one of these envelopes — is `instanceof ResponseEnvelope` reliable, and where does the exact revalidation header name come from?
must_include: respond(value, init?) / redirect(url, init?) / reload(init?) all return a ResponseEnvelope — an in-memory value paired with HTTP response metadata (status/headers/revalidate); redirect defaults to 302, reload carries no value and just requests revalidation

check envelopes with isResponseEnvelope(v), never instanceof ResponseEnvelope — it's a registered-symbol brand specifically so it survives separately bundled client/server copies of the class; instanceof can silently fail across bundles
import REVALIDATE_HEADER from the root @solidjs/web entry instead of hard-coding the X-Revalidate header name
questions.source: server-functions.md response helpers section

questions.title: affects() called outside an action does nothing visible
questions.prompt: I call `affects(todos)` from a plain click handler (no `action()` wrapping it) right before kicking off a fetch, expecting the list to read pending while the fetch runs. `isPending(() => todos.length)` never flips in the UI. Why, and where does `affects` belong?
must_include: an affects() mark is scoped to the surrounding transaction; called outside any transaction it is released at the end of the current flush, so it never reaches effects or the UI
put the affects() call inside an action() (the transaction), alongside the refresh()/awaited work, so the mark stays live until that transaction settles or reverts
questions.source: async-and-actions.md affects section

questions.title: reconcile default-id and positional modes
questions.prompt: What is the exact second argument of `reconcile(value, ...)`? Explain omitted, `null`, and missing-key behavior, plus what happens for an array/object shape mismatch and for a different root entity selected by the caller.
must_include: the signature is reconcile(value, key?) where key is a string, key extractor, or null — it is not the old 1.x options object
omitting key defaults to the "id" property; null selects fully positional merging; an item missing the selected key falls back to positional matching
an array/object shape mismatch replaces the nested slot rather than leaving the wrong proxy shape
standalone reconcile throws when asked to merge a different root entity into the caller-selected slot; authoritative returned-root replacement belongs to projections/derived stores
questions.source: stores.md:54-86; migration-map.md:174-193

questions.title: store shallow option overloads
questions.prompt: Importing store APIs from `solid-js`, which plain and derived `createStore` / `createOptimisticStore` overloads accept `{ shallow: true }` or `ProjectionOptions`? Is the broader `@solidjs/signals` plain optimistic overload safe to teach for a `solid-js` import?
must_include: plain createStore(initial, { name?, shallow? }) accepts shallow, while derived createStore(derive, seed, ProjectionOptions) accepts name/key/shallow
through the published solid-js client typings, plain createOptimisticStore(initial) accepts NO options; only its derived overload accepts ProjectionOptions
although @solidjs/signals declares a broader plain optimistic options overload, do not teach it for code importing from solid-js
questions.source: stores.md:31-52

questions.title: recursive JSX refs and applyRef typing
questions.prompt: A renderer library forwards nested Solid DOM refs. What shapes does `JSX.Ref<T>` allow, what is the generic `applyRef` signature, and which argument determines the concrete DOM element subtype?
must_include: JSX.Ref<T> is recursive: a direct T, a RefCallback<T>, undefined, or an array of Ref<T>, so nested ref arrays type-check
applyRef<T extends Element = Element> accepts one callback or an array of callbacks whose element parameter is NoInfer<T>, plus element: T, and returns void

the actual element argument determines T; NoInfer prevents callback annotations from choosing or widening it, and library code should use applyRef rather than React-style ref objects or manually invoking refs
questions.source: typescript-setup.md DOM ref typing and applyRef section

questions.title: claimElementTree is integration-only
questions.prompt: Should application code call `claimElementTree(root)` as a normal ref/hydration helper? What does Solid use it for, what descendants are claimed, and what does its server export do?
must_include: claimElementTree is low-level renderer/integration infrastructure for frames, routers, and adopted or streamed SSR DOM — not an application ref, hydration, or DOM initialization idiom
on the client it sweep-claims navigation-relevant descendants such as a[href] and form[action] when DOM arrives without compiled creation code; on the server it is a no-op
questions.source: control-flow-and-dom.md claimElementTree section

questions.title: built-in no-JS flash and redirect protocol
questions.prompt: A browser submits a Solid server-function form with JavaScript disabled. What does core do by default with truthy and falsy ordinary returned/thrown outcomes versus a returned/thrown `Response`, where does it redirect, and how can an integration replay or disable this behavior?
must_include: the built-in browser-form createNoJSHandler stores only a TRUTHY non-Response returned or thrown outcome in the one-shot flash cookie, then redirects to the request referer (or its configured base/fallback) with 303
a falsy outcome (0, false, empty string, null, or undefined) is not flashed because the runtime uses a truthiness guard; it still redirects, so the next render cannot replay that outcome
a returned or thrown Response is never flashed and preserves its headers and Location plus a valid redirect status; without a Location it redirects back

FLASH_COOKIE, hasFlashCookie, and clearFlashCookie are isomorphic exports; encodeFlashCookie/decodeFlashCookie/createNoJSHandler are server exports, and the cookie must be cleared on the following render even if decode fails

a custom handleNoJS is required for falsy-safe replay; a per-request handleNoJS overrides the configured/default handler, while server config may install a custom handler or set handleNoJS to null to disable the convention and return the normal serialized response
flash payloads are JSON and cookie-sized (roughly 4 KB); FormData/URLSearchParams become entry pairs and files are dropped
questions.source: server-functions.md No-JS progressive enhancement section

questions.title: server-function transport integration seams
questions.prompt: An integration must send Date/Map arguments and consume a custom response/single-flight envelope. What is the standard rich-argument opt-in, which client hooks consume custom responses, is `codec` alone enough, what does `decodeResponsePayload` return, which server-side transform hooks mirror the integration, and what complete set of fields does `ServerFunctionOutcome` provide?
must_include: default argument lists are JSON-safe only (apart from a single natively encoded body); Date, Map, Set, typed arrays, cycles and similar rich values require calling enableRichArguments() from @solidjs/web/server-functions/rich-args — importing that entry installs serializeArgs and opts the bundle into the encoder; codec alone is not enough
responseHandler.capture runs synchronously at the call site and responseHandler.handle sees each response before normal decoding; a non-undefined return becomes the call result
decodeResponsePayload(response) returns { value, flightData? } and separates the single-flight envelope
server config exposes transformResult and transformDirectResult, with per-request transformResult overriding the configured default

ServerFunctionOutcome provides the complete set id, value, response, request, thrown, targetUrl, revalidateKeys, and foldedHeaders; targetUrl is the same-origin outcome Location or otherwise the referer, revalidateKeys are split, foldedHeaders include Set-Cookie effects, and foldSetCookies exposes the same cookie-folding operation for custom collection
questions.source: server-functions.md transport integration and single-flight sections

questions.title: experimental frames surface and stability
questions.prompt: Are Solid server components part of the stable 2.0 contract? Which package subpaths contain the client/server frame APIs, and name the key client and server integration exports without using the retired marker-range APIs.
must_include: server components are an experimental preview outside Solid 2.0 stability guarantees and their versions should be pinned
the conditional entry is @solidjs/web/frames, with explicit @solidjs/web/frames/client and @solidjs/web/frames/server subpaths

client exports include installServerComponents, createFrameHost/createFrameElement, applyFrameResponse and isFrameStreamResponse; server exports include renderServerComponent, serverComponentResponse, frameTransformResult and frameTransformDirectResult, with Slot available on both sides
questions.source: server-components.md introduction and stream ownership sections

questions.title: Promise of AsyncIterable flattening
questions.prompt: A server function returns `Promise<AsyncIterable<Message>>`, and a memo returns that promise directly. Does the memo settle to the iterable object, or stream it? Is a `yield* await serverFn()` adapter required?
must_include: Solid flattens the Promise<AsyncIterable> as one async computation and streams the iterable; each yielded item becomes a committed memo value
no yield* await adapter is required
questions.source: async-and-actions.md async lives in computations section

questions.title: fully settled SSR string
questions.prompt: How do you obtain a fully settled async HTML string in @solidjs/web 2.0 rc.3? Does `renderToStringAsync` exist, and can you also pipe/read the same render after awaiting it?
must_include: renderToStringAsync does not exist; use await renderToStream(code, options), because the returned stream is PromiseLike<string> and awaiting it yields the fully settled HTML
the render has one consumer: choose await, pipe(), pipeTo(), or readable; mixing distinct consumers throws
questions.source: control-flow-and-dom.md rendering entries section

questions.title: server-function security defaults
questions.prompt: What happens to a plain Error thrown by a production server function, how do you intentionally expose a safe client-facing error, and what same-origin/CSRF protection does the handler apply by default?
must_include: outside the development build condition, plain thrown values are sanitized to a generic Error("Internal Server Error") without the original message, stack, or own properties; the build variant, not NODE_ENV, selects this
use respond(...) / a thrown envelope, or markSafeError(error) from @solidjs/web for intentional client-facing error content; isSafeError is the cross-bundle-safe check
server-function HTTP calls have same-origin csrf protection enabled by default; csrf: false is only for an endpoint already protected by another trusted layer
questions.source: server-functions.md runtime split and thrown errors sections

questions.title: server setter writes are deprecated
questions.prompt: During SSR, code writes a signal, a store, and an optimistic store from subscription callbacks. What happens today, and what model should replace those writes?
must_include: server setter writes emit a [SERVER_WRITE] deprecation warning once per process/category and are intended to become errors
signal and store writes only change inert data for later reads/serialization and never re-render; optimistic writes are complete no-ops and their setter callback does not run
model server changes as async computation sources; return a subscription as an AsyncIterable instead of pushing through setters
questions.source: reactivity.md server rendering is setter-free section

questions.title: diagnostics harness
questions.prompt: For an automated reactivity regression test, what published package captures structured diagnostics and recompute budgets instead of scraping console output? Name the core capture helper and representative assertions.
must_include: use @solidjs/diagnostics and captureArtifact() for a serializable diagnostic/attribution artifact
assert with expectDiagnostic / expectNoDiagnostics and recompute or waste budgets with expectRerunBudget / expectNoWaste; dedicated vitest, browser, and playwright entries are available
questions.source: reactivity.md dev diagnostics section

questions.title: RequestEventLocals module augmentation
questions.prompt: How should an app type custom `getRequestEvent()!.locals.user` data in Solid 2.0, and what declaration-file shape accidentally replaces package types instead of augmenting them?
must_include: augment interface RequestEventLocals in declare module "@solidjs/web"; that shared interface flows to RequestEvent.locals
the declaration must itself be a module (top-level import or export {}); a global script-style declare module block defines/replaces the ambient module instead of augmenting the package
questions.source: server-functions.md RequestEvent and request scoping section

questions.title: measure-then-position (createRenderEffect)
questions.prompt: You portal a tooltip panel into document.body and must measure it with getBoundingClientRect() then set its top/left. Which effect do you use, and where do you read the geometry — inside the `ref` callback or somewhere else? Why is the measurement correct?
must_include: use createRenderEffect (the render-lane / useLayoutEffect analog) for measure-then-write-layout

do NOT read getBoundingClientRect in the ref callback (the node may be pre-insert / pre-layout there); stash the node in a signal via ref={setNode} and read geometry inside the effect keyed on that signal
by the time the effect runs in the flush the node is already inserted into the DOM, so getBoundingClientRect reads true geometry — NOT zeros
questions.source: reactivity.md createRenderEffect and lane selection sections

questions.title: paint timing — no flash
questions.prompt: If you used createEffect instead of createRenderEffect to position that tooltip, would the user see a visible flash of the panel at the wrong spot before it jumps into place? Explain the paint timing precisely, and give the real reason to prefer the render lane.
must_include: NO visible flash — both the render lane and the user lane run in the SAME microtask flush, before the browser paints
createEffect is NOT post-paint like React's useEffect; Solid has no post-paint effect phase
the real reason to prefer createRenderEffect for layout is PHASE CORRECTNESS (lockstep with DOM, before user-lane consumers, not deferred by Suspense/hydration), not avoiding a flicker
questions.source: reactivity.md createRenderEffect paint timing section

questions.title: list rendering with For
questions.prompt: Render a list of todos keyed by identity. Then show how you would render it index-keyed (the old <Index> behavior). Note the callback shapes.
must_include: use <For each={...}> — default/keyed={true} keys by identity, callback is (rawItem, indexAccessor) so the index is called i()
index-keyed is <For keyed={false}> with callback (itemAccessor, plainIndex) — item is called item(), index is a plain number
questions.source: control-flow-and-dom.md:8-27

questions.title: store nested update
questions.prompt: Update a nested store field `user.name` and push an item to `list` in one store. Show the import and the setter call.
must_include: store APIs (createStore, etc.) import from 'solid-js' — the solid-js/store subpath is gone
setter takes a draft you mutate in place: setStore(s => { s.user.name = 'B'; s.list.push(x); }) — produce is the default, no produce() import
questions.source: stores.md:1-29

questions.title: cancel an in-flight fetch on re-run
questions.prompt: A memo `createMemo(async () => fetchUser(id()))` re-runs when `id()` changes. Does Solid cancel the previous in-flight request for you? Show how to abort it on a re-run and on dispose.
must_include: Solid does NOT auto-cancel the in-flight request — it discards the superseded value but the request keeps running; you cancel it yourself with an AbortController
create the AbortController in the compute and register onCleanup(() => ac.abort()) synchronously (before the await), passing ac.signal to fetch — on a re-run or on dispose the previous request aborts
questions.source: async-and-actions.md cancellation and cleanup section

questions.title: stream a socket through an async-gen memo and clean it up
questions.prompt: Stream messages from a WebSocket through `createMemo(async function* () { … })` so each message updates the accessor. How do you tear the socket down on dispose, and why isn't a `try/finally` inside the generator enough?
must_include: yield* a bridge over the socket's messages so each message commits; register the teardown with onCleanup synchronously BEFORE the first await/yield — after a suspension point there is no owner (NO_OWNER_CLEANUP) and the cleanup never runs
the onCleanup must actively close the socket / cancel the source — this both frees it AND unblocks the parked await so the generator can unwind

try/finally is NOT reliable: on dispose Solid DOES call .return() on the iterator, but a generator parked on an external await won't unwind — .return() queues behind that await and finally won't run until it settles, which for a silent socket is never
questions.source: patterns.md streaming socket section; async-and-actions.md async generator cleanup section

questions.title: bare refresh() is a silent same-question re-ask; optimistic writes are verdict-inert
questions.prompt: An action does an optimistic `createOptimisticStore` write, then `yield`s the server call, then `refresh(todos)`. You try to show a `Saving…` spinner with `<Show when={isPending(() => todos())}>` — but it never appears. Why doesn't isPending report the in-flight save, and how do you show the saving state correctly?
must_include: the optimistic write is verdict-inert: it doesn't read pending on its own slot and it does not mask anything else

the real reason isPending stays false is that a bare refresh(todos) is a silent, same-question re-ask: it doesn't change the tracked input (the query key), so it reveals the fresh value without ever flipping isPending to true — this is true whether or not an optimistic write is live

drive the Saving… affordance from co-written data instead: a flag pushed into the optimistic write itself (e.g. { ...todo, pending: true }), or a separate createOptimistic(false) flag read by value — not via isPending; if the reload itself should read as pending, declare it explicitly: affects(todos); refresh(todos)
questions.source: async-and-actions.md isPending and optimistic sections

questions.title: onSettled cleanup only in an owned scope
questions.prompt: Inside an event handler (not the component body) you call `onSettled(() => { const off = subscribe(); return () => off(); })`. Does that returned cleanup run, and where should setup-with-teardown live instead?
must_include: a returned cleanup from onSettled is only honored in an OWNED scope (a component body); fired out of band — from an event handler, a tracked effect, or another onSettled — there is no owner to bind to, so returning a cleanup is a dev error (SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED) and is dropped in production
the out-of-band one-shot fire with no cleanup is fine (e.g. onSettled(() => toast('Saved')) after a handler write); for setup-with-teardown, call the helper from the component body instead
questions.source: reactivity.md onSettled section; migration-map.md lifecycle rename row

questions.title: store-in-store structural tracking
questions.prompt: A derived store returns an inner store, and `<For each={outer.items}>` renders it. After the inner store is reconciled, direct reads show fresh rows but an older release left `<For>` stale. What is the current contract for `<For>`/`mapArray`, `Object.keys`, `snapshot`, and `deep` through this wrapper? Should you clone the inner store as a workaround?
must_include: structural tracking chains through the outer wrapper to the inner store, so reconcile/add/delete invalidates <For>/mapArray and Object.keys as well as snapshot/deep
structural consumers and direct property reads now stay consistent; the stale optimistic row bug through a wrapper is fixed
do NOT clone the inner store as a workaround; preserve the fine-grained store view
questions.source: stores.md store-in-store views section

questions.title: lazy SSR identity and hydration
questions.prompt: An SSR app creates a lazy component from an `import.meta.glob` entry, so the `lazy()` callsite has no static `moduleUrl`. How does Solid hydrate it, how does the server find the asset identity, and what is `Lazy.moduleUrl` during that SSR request? Contrast that getter with a callsite that does supply `moduleUrl`, and show the supported way to select a named export. What happens if no identity exists at all?
must_include: the client matches preloaded lazy modules positionally by HYDRATION ID, not module identity, so a callsite without moduleUrl can hydrate
the server waits for the import and uses the module's bundler-injected $$moduleUrl export when the callsite has no moduleUrl
for this glob callsite Lazy.moduleUrl remains undefined even after $$moduleUrl is loaded; $$moduleUrl is used only for deferred asset registration and does not populate the component getter
manifest resolution, modulepreload-on-access, and the raw-specifier fallback apply to Lazy.moduleUrl only when the lazy() callsite supplied moduleUrl
if neither moduleUrl nor $$moduleUrl exists, SSR still renders and WARNS about a late client load instead of throwing
select a named export with lazy(() => import(...), { export: "Name" }); the export name is a call-site literal, and moduleUrl is now the third argument
questions.source: control-flow-and-dom.md lazy SSR and hydration section

questions.title: action yield/await contract — writes after await, before yield, escape the transaction
questions.prompt: Inside `action(async function* (todo) { const res = await api.save(todo); setOptimisticTodos(s => { s.push(todo); }); refresh(todos); return res; })` the write and refresh() happen right after the `await`, with no `yield` in between. Is that write transaction-safe? What's the fix?
must_include: no — yield is the ONLY transaction-safe suspension point (ruled behaves-as-designed); writes made between an internal await and the next yield escape the action's transition and land un-batched, outside the optimistic/reconcile coordination around them
fix: await for the value, insert a bare yield to re-enter the transaction, THEN do the write/refresh — await api.save(todo); yield; setOptimisticTodos(...); refresh(todos); return res;
questions.source: async-and-actions.md action yield and await contract section

questions.title: Portal is a client-only island
questions.prompt: An app wraps a dialog in `<Portal mount={modalRoot}><Loading fallback={<Spinner />}><Dialog /></Loading></Portal>`. Does the server render the Dialog's markup? Does async work started inside the portal show up in an ancestor Loading boundary outside the portal? Where should a read that must happen on the server live?
must_include: the server renders nothing for <Portal> — its children never evaluate, no async starts inside it, and nothing is serialized for that subtree
the portal's children render fresh on the client (under hydration nothing is claimed for them), so async started inside the portal begins on the client — it is not server-fetched
async discovered after settle forwards through already-initialized ancestor boundaries as ordinary pending status rather than dropping any of them back into fallback
a read that must run on the server belongs ABOVE the portal — hoist it out; the portal itself won't run it server-side
questions.source: control-flow-and-dom.md Portal section

questions.title: shallow store updates and list identity
questions.prompt: A shallow store contains rows. Why does `setRows(d => { d[0].label = "new" })` fail to notify, what update works, how does `reconcile` behave at that boundary, and how should rebuilt rows preserve DOM identity?
must_include: shallow true makes only root properties or array slots reactive; nested records are raw, so mutating a nested field in place is reactively invisible
replace the root property or array slot with a new record reference
reconcile compares nested records by reference at a shallow boundary and replaces changed root slots instead of recursively mutating raw records
if refreshes rebuild row objects, preserve DOM identity at the consumer with <For keyed={row => row.id}>
questions.source: stores.md shallow stores section

questions.title: projection authoritative root swap
questions.prompt: A `createProjection`/derived store switches from one root entity to another after the source key changes. Should it throw like standalone `reconcile`, and which descendants survive the switch?
must_include: a returned new root from createProjection, derived createStore, or derived createOptimisticStore is authoritative: the root entity swaps and descendants of the old root do not survive
this deliberately differs from standalone reconcile, which is strict when the caller targets a different root entity
questions.source: stores.md derived stores section

questions.title: native objects in stores remain raw
questions.prompt: A store slot holds a `Map`, and another holds a user class instance. What is reactive, should `map.set()` notify, are all class instances raw, and can you import `markRaw` from `solid-js`?
must_include: platform/native host objects such as Map, Date, DOM nodes and Headers are raw by default; reassigning their store slot is reactive but internal mutation such as map.set is not
replace the slot with a new object reference when consumers must update
user-defined class instances remain wrappable (unless frozen), so not every non-plain object is raw
markRaw is internal and is not a public solid-js root export; use shallow stores or reference replacement instead
questions.source: stores.md raw platform objects section

questions.title: lazy async memo survives observer gaps
questions.prompt: A started lazy async memo temporarily loses its last subscriber, then gains one before the request settles. Does Solid restart/dispose the work? Contrast this with a synchronous or already-settled lazy memo, explain what happens if async work settles unobserved, and say whether iterator release eliminates the need for explicit resource cleanup.
must_include: a synchronous or already-settled lazy memo autodisposes after losing its final subscriber and recomputes from scratch on the next read; a pending async memo is the exception
temporary loss of the final subscriber does not dispose a pending lazy async computation; a subscriber that returns before settlement rejoins the same in-flight work rather than starting a duplicate
if the computation settles while still unobserved, normal teardown resumes

Solid releases/closes an unobserved AsyncIterable, but deterministic external cleanup still belongs in a synchronous onCleanup before the first await/yield (AbortController, socket close, or iterator unblock/close)
questions.source: async-and-actions.md lazy async memo section; reactivity.md memo options section; patterns.md demand-driven resource section

questions.title: SSR dynamic/lazy shell gating
questions.prompt: During streaming SSR, a pending `dynamic()`/`lazy()` component is rendered once inside `<Loading>` and once as an unbounded root hole. When can the first shell flush and where does resolved content appear?
must_include: inside Loading, the pending component no longer gates the first shell: the fallback is emitted in the shell and resolved content streams later
without a boundary, the root hole still gates the first shell; the server waits and emits the resolved component inline rather than flushing an empty shell
questions.source: control-flow-and-dom.md SSR pending dynamic lazy section

questions.title: experimental server component setup and ownership
questions.prompt: Show the current shape for a server component with a client-owned slot: how is it declared and consumed, what must run before hydrate/render, which Vite flag enables it, what state survives refetch, what happens to app Context at the server-component root, and what DOM seam must CSS account for?
must_include: a server component is a component function returned by a server function; the client consumes its promise with dynamic(() => serverFn(...)) and passes client-owned positions as Slot props
call installServerComponents() explicitly before hydrate() or render(); a bare import is insufficient because the package is side-effect-free
enable @solidjs/vite-plugin with serverFunctions: { components: true }
the plugin wires endpoint frame responses; turnkey SSR also wires document rendering/adoption, while authored entries must install the frame render/bootstrap/client pieces themselves
server-owned HTML morphs in place while client-owned slot DOM identity and state survive updates; optional $key gives slot occurrence identity across reordering
the current boundary is a real dx-frame data-fid custom element, not an invisible marker range, so its inline-by-default CSS/layout seam must be handled
app Context does not cross a server-component root: default-less useContext throws, defaulted context reads its default, and providers created inside the server component work normally
questions.source: server-components.md declaration setup stream and footguns sections

questions.title: props are not destructured
questions.prompt: Write a component that receives a `title` prop and renders it in an <h1>. Call out any reactivity pitfall a React developer would hit.
must_include:
read props.title INSIDE the JSX — function Good(props) { return

{props.title}

}
do NOT destructure props in the parameter list and do NOT read props at the top level of the body — it captures once, goes stale, and warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED

questions.title: component runs once, no re-render
questions.prompt: In Solid 2.0, how many times does a component function execute, and when do effects re-run relative to 'renders'? Contrast explicitly with React's re-render-on-every-update model.
must_include: the component function runs exactly ONCE — there is no re-render and no virtual DOM
effects re-run only when their tracked dependencies change; the effect's compute phase IS the dependency declaration (no deps array)

questions.title: pass a signal to a child
questions.prompt: Given `const [count, setCount] = createSignal(0)`, pass count to a child <Counter> that displays it. Show both the call site and how the child reads it.
must_include: call the accessor at the JSX boundary: <Counter value={count()} /> — pass the VALUE, not the accessor function
the child reads props.value inside JSX (no destructuring); this keeps reactivity because the compiled JSX prop is a getter that re-runs count() in the child's tracking scope

questions.title: translate useState + useEffect
questions.prompt: Translate this React snippet to idiomatic Solid 2.0: `const [n, setN] = useState(0); useEffect(() => { document.title = String(n); }, [n]);`
must_include: useState(0) becomes createSignal(0)
useEffect becomes the SPLIT createEffect: createEffect(() => n(), v => { document.title = String(v); }) — compute reads n(), apply does the side effect
the dependency array [n] disappears — the compute phase tracks deps automatically

questions.title: composable naming — create* vs use*
questions.prompt: In Solid, what is the difference between naming a composable `createX` versus `useX` (for example `createPrefersDark` vs `usePrefersDark`)? When do you pick each?
must_include: createX creates a NEW reactive primitive owned by/scoped to the calling reactive scope — a fresh independent instance per call (the default)

useX accesses something already created and SHARED, not a fresh instance: either a context (useContext) or the singleton variant of a createX primitive (created once in a singleton/detached root and reused across callers)
questions.source: conventions.md:7-38; verified from @solid-primitives source: useWindowSize = createHydratableSingletonRoot(createWindowSize); usePrefersDark = createHydratableSingletonRoot(createPrefersDark); rationale solidjs/solid#317

questions.title: batch removed
questions.prompt: Batch these two writes together in Solid 2.0: `setA(1); setB(2);`. Show the idiomatic code.
must_include: batch() does NOT exist in 2.0 — batching is the default, so you just write setA(1); setB(2); with no wrapper
flush() is only needed if you must synchronously read your own writes right after
questions.source: reactivity.md:18; migration-map.md:41-49

questions.title: onMount equivalent
questions.prompt: What is the Solid 2.0 equivalent of `onMount` for component setup that adds a window resize listener and removes it on cleanup? Show it.
must_include: use onSettled(() => { ...; return cleanup }) in the component body — it replaces onMount and, in this owned scope, honors a returned cleanup (runs on owner disposal)
onSettled is a leaf owner: you cannot create reactive primitives or call onCleanup inside it — return a cleanup function instead
questions.source: reactivity.md onSettled section; migration-map.md lifecycle rename row

questions.title: imports moved
questions.prompt: In Solid 2.0, where do `render`, `Portal`, and `createStore` come from, what replaced `classList`, and what compiler packages replaced `babel-preset-solid`?
must_include: render and Portal import from '@solidjs/web' (NOT solid-js/web)
createStore (and other store APIs) import from 'solid-js' (NOT solid-js/store)
classList is gone — use the object/array form of the class prop: class={{ active: isActive() }}
babel-preset-solid is gone: use @solidjs/babel-plugin in Babel pipelines, or @solidjs/vite-plugin in Vite (which uses the native @solidjs/compiler by default)
questions.source: migration-map.md import paths; typescript-setup.md import paths and compiler paragraph; control-flow-and-dom.md class section

questions.title: createSelector replacement
questions.prompt: You need a derived store that marks the selected row id without notifying every row in the list. Which 1.x API did this, and what replaces it in 2.0?
must_include: the 1.x API was createSelector — it is gone in 2.0
the replacement is createProjection (a readonly derived store whose derive fn mutates a draft), which updates fine-grained without notifying the whole collection
questions.source: stores.md derived stores section; migration-map.md createSelector row

questions.title: 1.x resource.loading during refetch vs 2.0 refresh()
questions.prompt: In Solid 1.x, calling `refetch()` on a `createResource` flips `resource.loading` to true while the request is in flight, so a `<Show when={resource.loading}>` spinner shows during every refetch. Does the 2.0 equivalent — calling `refresh(todos)` — flip `isPending(() => todos())` to true the same way? If not, how do you recover the old always-shows-a-spinner-during-refetch behavior?
must_include: no — a bare refresh(todos) is a silent, same-question re-ask: it reveals the fresh value without ever flipping isPending to true, unlike 1.x resource.loading which was true for every refetch
to get the old always-pending-during-refetch behavior back, declare it explicitly: affects(todos); refresh(todos) — this makes the reload read as pending
questions.source: async-and-actions.md isPending and affects sections; migration-map.md resource loading row
